_problem:
packages/db/schema.ts declares 63 named CHECK constraints. An unknown but large fraction of them DO NOT EXIST in a migrated database under the declared name. Migrations 0002 through 0008 wrote their CHECKs INLINE and UNNAMED, so PostgreSQL auto-named them: sessions_vis_chk is really sessions_visibility_check, sessions_slots_chk is really sessions_slots_max_check, and so on. MEASURED FROM pg_constraint at 81b4fe8 on a database migrated to 0024: 47 auto-named CHECK constraints across 27 tables, against 25 correctly declared — so 47 of 72, roughly two thirds of every CHECK in the schema, do not exist under the name schema.ts spells.

That number replaces an earlier static count of 27-across-23 that this manifest originally carried. The static count came from awk-ing CHECK lines out of CREATE TABLE blocks in 0002-0008, and it was wrong twice over: it undercounted per-table CHECKs, and it rested on a claim that the auth-lane migrations named theirs correctly. They do not — auth_email_deliveries_kind_check, auth_email_tokens_purpose_check, auth_oauth_transactions_provider_check, channel_identities_platform_check and persons_status_check are all auto-named. The drift is repo-wide, not confined to the foundation layer. The correction is recorded rather than quietly swapped because it is the same failure this slice exists to fix: a number that reads as a fact because it is specific, produced by counting the declaration rather than the applied state.

This is a KNOWN bug class in this repo that was fixed in exactly one place and never swept. 0014:44-50 documents it verbatim for players — 'Postgres auto-named it players_status_check — NOT the players_status_chk spelled in schema.ts's Drizzle builder (that name was never applied to a live database)' — and fixes it with DROP IF EXISTS + ADD CONSTRAINT under the declared name. That fix was never applied to the other 26 tables.

It is NOT a correctness bug today: every constraint fires and enforces its predicate correctly under its auto-generated name. It is a trap for everything that comes after. Any migration, test or tool that assumes a schema.ts name literally exists in the database is wrong, and this has already bitten twice: db-public-visibility-capacity-check's PVC-3 discovered it while writing tests, and the reviewer's own Verdict 25 asserted two of those names as facts 'measured' when what was measured was schema.ts's source text. The autopilot dep_checks mechanism cannot catch it by construction — scope-gate resolves dep_checks with `git show <ref>:<file>` plus grep, so for a database object it cannot distinguish DECLARED from APPLIED.

ONE MORE DISCREPANCY THE CATALOG QUERY SURFACED, unresolved and deliberately not resolved here: schema.ts declares 63 named check() constraints, the database holds 72, and only 25 of the declared names exist. Renaming 47 auto-named constraints to their declared names would leave 72 total with 72 declared — but 63 declarations cannot cover 72 constraints. So either some live CHECKs have no schema.ts counterpart, or some declarations describe constraints that were never applied at all, or both. That gap is a finding for the design probe to quantify, not something to paper over during a rename.

P1 rather than the P2 the backlog first assumed, for one reason: four of the 27 affected tables are money-path — charges (4 CHECKs), bank_transactions (4), payment_allocations (3), bank_accounts (2), 13 constraints in all. A future money-path slice writing a migration or an invariant test against charges_* names would be silently wrong on the money path specifically.
_decision_contract: 0014 is the settled precedent and this slice mirrors it rather than inventing a shape: DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS <auto_name>, DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS <declared_name> as belt-and-braces, then ADD CONSTRAINT <declared_name> CHECK (<identical predicate>). Predicates do not change. No column changes, no nullability changes, no RLS or grant changes. Every rename is a pure identity change so that schema.ts and pg_constraint finally agree. Migrations 0000-0024 stay byte-identical; the whole sweep is ONE new monotonic migration. 0024's sessions_public_capacity_chk is already correctly named and MUST NOT be touched.
_scope_in: One module, packages/db. Exactly ONE monotonic migration after the live tail (0025 at authoring baseline 0024) renaming auto-generated CHECK constraint names to the names schema.ts declares, for whatever set the design probe pins. Plus a REGRESSION TEST that makes this class of drift impossible to reintroduce silently — the point of the slice is not only to fix the ones counted today, it is to ensure the next one cannot appear unnoticed.
_scope_out: NO predicate change of any kind — a rename that also alters what a constraint accepts is a different slice and a money-path risk. NO column, nullability, default or type change. NO RLS, role or grant change. NO edit to applied migrations 0000-0024. NO touching sessions_public_capacity_chk (0024, already correctly named). NO apps/bot or apps/web file — this runs in PARALLEL with job-schedule-outbox-dispatch, which holds retry-liveness, and any shared file or token collides. NO drizzle-kit regeneration of schema.ts: schema.ts's declared names are the TARGET, not the thing to change.
_design_probe:
Required per canonical autopilot-prompt-GENERIC v0.6.1 §0.1 — trigger (7) schema/migration and (6) amends merged core tables, several of them money-path. Before any production edit, write .autopilot/state/db-check-constraint-naming-drift/design-probe.md pinning FOUR things and STOP for founder confirm.

(a) SCOPE — the decision this slice exists to make, and the one a mechanical mirror will get wrong by trusting the backlog note. The backlog entry that opened this said 'sessions' five constraints'. That was written from what PVC-3 happened to touch, not from a measurement. The real extent, measured from pg_constraint on a database migrated to 0024, is 47 auto-named CHECKs across 27 tables out of 72 total. An earlier static file count in this manifest said 27-across-23 and was wrong — treat that as a warning about method, not a second opinion. So the question is not how to rename sessions' — it is whether this slice sweeps ALL 47, or only the money-path subset, or a smaller boundary. Re-run the catalog query yourself and state your own number; if it disagrees with 47, the catalog wins again and you say so. A partial sweep leaves the identical trap live for every table it skips, and the next author rediscovers it the same way this one was rediscovered.

(b) DERIVE THE AUTO-NAMES, DO NOT GUESS THEM. PostgreSQL's auto-naming is <table>_<column>_check for a column constraint and <table>_check for a table constraint, with a numeric suffix on collision — so a table with two unnamed table-level CHECKs has sessions_check and sessions_check1, and which is which depends on declaration order. Do NOT hand-write the list from the pattern. Query pg_constraint on a freshly migrated database and pin the real (conname, pg_get_constraintdef) pairs, then match each to its schema.ts counterpart BY PREDICATE, not by guessing which name maps to which. Record any constraint where the live predicate and the schema.ts predicate DIFFER — that is a separate finding and is out of scope to fix here, but must not be silently renamed over.

(c) THE MONEY-PATH SUBSET. charges, bank_transactions, payment_allocations and bank_accounts carry 13 of the 47. A DROP followed by an ADD inside one transaction is atomic, so there is no window where a money table is unconstrained — verify that migrate.ts really does run each file in a single transaction rather than assuming it, then state it. If any money-path predicate turns out to differ between live and schema.ts, HALT and report rather than reconciling it inside a rename slice.

(d) HOW THE 28TH IS PREVENTED. A rename sweep that ships without a guard is a fix with a shelf life — 0014 fixed one table and the class came back. Propose the guard: a test that asserts every check() name declared in schema.ts exists in pg_constraint, or the inverse, or both. Say what it costs on each future migration and where it fails loudly. This item is not optional garnish; without it the slice is a one-time cleanup of a recurring defect.

(e) THE 63-VERSUS-72 GAP, added after the catalog measurement. schema.ts declares 63 named check() constraints; pg_constraint holds 72 in the public schema, of which only 25 carry a declared-style name. Those numbers cannot all be reconciled by renaming: 63 declarations do not cover 72 constraints. Quantify it — list any live CHECK with no schema.ts counterpart, and any schema.ts declaration with no live constraint at all. Both are real findings. The second is worse than a naming drift: it means a constraint someone believes is enforced does not exist. Report them; do not rename over them and do not add missing constraints in this slice.
_acceptance: CND-1: for every constraint in the pinned scope, the schema.ts-declared name EXISTS in pg_constraint after migration — asserted by querying the catalog, never by grepping schema.ts. This is the entire point: the old assertion method is what hid the bug.

CND-2: for every constraint in the pinned scope, the auto-generated name NO LONGER exists — a rename that leaves both is a duplicate constraint, doubling enforcement cost and confusing every future reader.
CND-3: PREDICATE IDENTITY — for each renamed constraint, pg_get_constraintdef before and after are semantically identical. Capture before-state in the test, not from this manifest's prose.

CND-4: BEHAVIOURAL REGRESSION, not just catalog inspection — for each renamed constraint, attempt the violation it exists to reject and assert it still fails, and attempt a valid write and assert it still succeeds. A catalog-only assertion would pass even if a predicate were mangled during transcription.
CND-5: money-path tables (charges, bank_transactions, payment_allocations, bank_accounts) get CND-4 coverage explicitly and individually, not as part of a loop that could skip a case silently.
CND-6: sessions_public_capacity_chk from 0024 is untouched and still present under its original name.

CND-7: THE 28TH IS BLOCKED — the guard pinned in design-probe item (d) exists and FAILS when a new unnamed CHECK is introduced. Prove it by adding a deliberately unnamed CHECK in the test and asserting the guard catches it. A guard that has never been seen to fail is not a guard.
CND-8: migrations 0000-0024 are byte-identical after 0025 applies, and the migration-count assertions advance 25 -> 26 in BOTH places that assert them.
CND-9: no RLS policy, role, grant, column, type or nullability changed — assert structurally against the migration diff.
CND-10: full workspace suite green; the DB suite count increases only by the tests this slice adds.

CND-11: the 63-versus-72 gap is quantified and reported — every live CHECK with no schema.ts counterpart, and every schema.ts declaration with no live constraint, listed by name in the probe and carried into the READY report. A schema.ts declaration with NO live constraint is a believed-but-absent guard and must be named explicitly, not folded into the rename count.
_scope_exception: Runs in PARALLEL with job-schedule-outbox-dispatch. Verified rather than assumed: this slice is packages/db only with invariants [schema]; that slice is apps/bot only with [retry-liveness]. Empty file intersection, empty invariant intersection, so neither scope-gate collision branch fires. It also does NOT collide with docs-session-capacity-chk-landed-reconcile on files, but DOES share the `schema` token with it — those two must run sequentially relative to each other.
_evidence_rules: Re-verify on synced main before coding, by measuring rather than trusting this manifest: run the pg_constraint query yourself against a freshly migrated database and derive the real auto-generated names and predicates. This manifest's count of 47 across 27 tables was measured from pg_constraint at 81b4fe8 on a database migrated to 0024. An earlier revision claimed 27-across-23 from static file analysis and was wrong by twenty, including a false claim that the auth-lane migrations name theirs correctly — they do not. If your catalog query disagrees with 47, the catalog wins and you say so in the probe. Read 0014:44-50 and :78-80 verbatim; that comment is both the precedent and the proof this class recurs. Confirm the live migration tail is 0024 before numbering 0025. Do not modify an applied migration to make numbering tidy, and do not let a rename become a predicate edit.
